nodes.label: The Self-Driving Walk (record-free aufbau chain)
nodes.rationale: config(Z+1) = config(Z) + the electron in the channel minimising E_HF; the reference is the previous neutral rather than ground(Z) minus an entrant, so nothing is read from the observed record past the declared seed config(1)=1s(1). Written because the existing drivers (nlwalk_hf.entrant, hf_chan.py) compute the entrant as ground.expand(Z) minus ground.expand(Z-1) and are therefore told the answer and then check it.

nodes.label: Literature above Z=108 as comparison column, never input
nodes.rationale: Desclaux 1973, Fricke/Greiner/Waber 1971, Pyykko 2011 and ADNDT 2016 all supply energies for an ASSUMED configuration (Madelung where stated), so importing any of them hands the walk the ordering the walk exists to produce. Refused on that ground, not on a provenance-label ground: RECALLED-NOT-ENTERED.

nodes.label: Candidate channel rule (occupancy and node condition only)
nodes.rationale: c = (n,l) with occ(c) < 2(2l+1), n <= N+1, l <= min(n-1,4). N+1 admits a new shell (without it Ne could never reach 3s); l<=4 admits g as a stated bound rather than an assumption. No n+l anywhere, and pruning by 'never observed' is refused because it imports the record.

nodes.label: First-divergence scoring of a chained walk
nodes.rationale: A chain has no reset, so one wrong entrant changes every configuration above it; after the first divergence the rows are not independent tests and a per-element tally would be dishonest. Two scores reported: chained from the seed, and restarted at each Z<=108 (which is the per-element test hf_chan already performs).

nodes.label: Three provenance classes above Z=108
nodes.rationale: OBSERVED (Z<=108, NIST ASD 5.12), SYNTHESISED-UNMEASURED (109-118: ground.py stops at 108 because the COLLECTION stops, not the subject), PREDICTED-UNSYNTHESISED (119-120, admitted at R 1656). Every chain output above 108 carries PREDICTED-BY-FIELD and names its own reference config.
